title: Common Cents Act
official_summary:
Common Cents Act

This bill ends the production of the penny for general circulation, requires rounding to an amount divisible by five for the payment or transfer of cash, and allows the nickel to be composed of different material.

The Department of the Treasury must stop producing the penny, except to meet collector needs. The penny shall continue to be legal tender.

Any person selling goods or services in a cash transaction, entering into other transfers of cash, or paying cash wages to an employee must round the payment up or down in accordance with the bill.

The bill also allows Treasury to discontinue the minting for circulation of any coin if Treasury follows procedures as outlined by the bill, including providing notice and a briefing to Congress.

The Federal Reserve Board must periodically report on a strategic plan for the acceptance of penny orders and deposits at commercial coin terminals that provide services under agreements with Federal Reserve banks. 

Finally, the bill allows for a different material composition of the nickel. In addition to being made from an alloy of copper and nickel, the nickel may also be clad with an inner core of zinc and an outer layer of nickel.

summary.headline: Law ends making pennies for everyday use and requires cash payments to be rounded to the nearest five cents.
summary.what_it_does: The Treasury must stop making pennies for general use, though it can still make them for collectors, and pennies remain legal money. Anyone paying or receiving cash, including stores and employers paying cash wages, must round the total up or down to an amount divisible by five, following the law's rules. The law also lets the Treasury stop minting other coins if it follows set steps, such as notifying and briefing Congress. It allows nickels to be made with a zinc core covered by nickel, in addition to the current copper-nickel mix.

who_it_affects.how: Their cash totals will be rounded up or down to the nearest amount divisible by five cents.
They must round cash sales according to the law's rounding rules.

who_it_affects.group: Employers who pay wages in cash
who_it_affects.how: They must round cash wage payments to an amount divisible by five.
Their cash wages will be rounded up or down under the law's rules.
The Treasury may still make pennies to meet collector demand.

who_it_affects.group: Banks and commercial coin terminals working with Federal Reserve banks
who_it_affects.how: The Federal Reserve must periodically report on a plan for accepting penny orders and deposits at these terminals.
They must stop making circulating pennies and may change nickel materials or stop minting other coins after notifying Congress.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 20, 2026; the summary does not give specific start dates for the rounding rules or the end of penny production.
